test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 26 July 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A train can completely cross a 1000-metre long bridge in 15 seconds. It can completely cross another 1300-metre long bridge in 19 seconds. What is the length of the train?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **bridge lengths** = 1300 − 1000 = 300 m.

Difference in **time taken** = 19 − 15 = 4 seconds.

**Speed of train** = 300 ÷ 4 = 75 m/s.

Total distance in 15 seconds = 75 × 15 = 1125 m.

**Length of train** = Total distance − Bridge length = 1125 − 1000 = 125 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 125 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5fa1a1568d25ba037ce1a1da150c0d69c488cc4df9afd912c31d038dcf121375.png] 

**Given:** Bridge₁ = 1000 m, T₁ = 15 s; Bridge₂ = 1300 m, T₂ = 19 s.

**Formula Used:** Speed = (Length of Train + Length of Bridge) ÷ Time

⇒ Let length of **Train** be L.

⇒ Speed = (L + 1000) ÷ 15 = (L + 1300) ÷ 19

⇒ 19 × (L + 1000) = 15 × (L + 1300)

⇒ 19L + 19000 = 15L + 19500

⇒ 19L − 15L = 19500 − 19000

⇒ 4L = 500

⇒ L = 125 m

**∴ The correct answer is 125 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Train crossing a stationary object with length

When a train crosses a **bridge, platform, or tunnel**, the total distance covered is the sum of the **length of the train** and the **length of the object**.

Train crossing a point object

When a train crosses a **pole, man, or tree**, the distance covered is equal to the **length of the train** itself (L = Speed × Time).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p
